Main reader imports backend functions and renamed publisher explicitly. Presentation source bindings use the renamed path. Root must stage deletion of the old website file and addition of the renamed publisher before the final commit.

findings.finding: The website publisher and benchmark loader previously shared qcb_nonlean_workbook basename. sys.path/sys.modules state could resolve the wrong module; the previous audit did not exercise fresh CLI/import startup. Root fixture evidence exposed the defect.
findings.resolution: Website publisher is now qcb_workbook_reader.py with no backend import at module load. Five independent fresh-process regressions pass, including both import orders and CLI --help.

findings.finding: Initial omitted reader-comparison hash keys could remove annotation protection.
findings.resolution: Exact seven-path binding-set check remains in the successor loader. Historical source-bound missing-all/missing-B-notation injection regressions reject on the preceding loader; inspected successor backend delta only adds groups to result. No new evidence-key omission is introduced.

findings.finding: New payload/review GitHub links must exist byte-identically at the actual publication commit.
findings.resolution: The existing check_publication_sources guard is retained and wired into main publish. Preintegration HEAD rejection is historical expected behavior. Actual committed candidate and production links require root gates.

findings.resolution: Prior effective-attribute, clean-filter and 147-index-blob equality checks support the report-only -text -eol rule. Normal benchmark source LF policy remains. No raw receipt was normalized or resealed by this worker.

Root owns full publication fixtures, actual browser geometry/MathJax/disclosures/search/graph behavior, full build, CI, merge and deployment. This report claims none of those gates passed.
limitations: Fresh import success does not prove full runtime/publication behavior. CLI --help is startup evidence only.
HTMLParser checks inspect static output and selected literal leakage, not rendered accessibility, layout, MathJax or live graph interaction.
Reviewer identity/hash presence does not establish external human approval or natural-language equivalence by itself; mathematical and notation reviews remain separate evidence.
